title: Do k-Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Thinking Patterns? Interpretable Features in a Small Reasoning Model
primary_claim: Pre-trained k-sparse autoencoders applied to DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B's hidden states (on GSM8K reasoning traces) successfully extract interpretable features, including several features in layer 10 that strongly and repeatedly activate on tokens characteristic of the model's reasoning process.
metric: frequency a feature is a top feature across 32 model inferences (layer 10)
target_value: feature 32456: top feature in 28/32 inferences; feature 6252: 14/32; feature 31146: 10/32

title: The REPHRASE Circuit: How Fine-Tuning Enhances LLMs to REPHRASE Text
primary_claim: Instruction fine-tuning enhances a specific attention head (L30H31) that performs copy suppression, and other heads including L13H(20-23), which together account for INSTRUCT's much better performance at the REPHRASE task compared to BASE (average logit difference 7.37 vs -1.02).

title: LLM Self-Reference Language in Multilingual vs English-Centric Models
primary_claim: Instruction tuning compresses attention-entropy-based self-referent processing toward neutral fact-retrieval processing in English-centric models (Llama, Mistral), while a multilingual model (Qwen) largely preserves the distinct attention pattern between self-referent and neutral prompts after instruction tuning.
metric: mean change in Role-Focus Coefficient (ΔRFC) from base to instruct, by model
target_value: Llama 3.1 8B: -0.023 (68.8% of layers compress); Mistral 7B: -0.093 (81.2% compress); Qwen 2.5 7B: +0.048 (28.6% compress, 50% near zero)

title: Automated Circuit Interpretation via Probe Prompting
primary_claim: An automated 'probe-prompting' pipeline that measures feature activation responses to concept-varying prompts and groups features into concept-aligned supernodes achieves 0.53 Replacement / 0.83 Completeness on Neuronpedia metrics for 'capitals' attribution-graph circuits in Gemma-2-2B, outperforming geometric (cosine-only, layer-adjacency) clustering baselines on behavioral-coherence interpretability metrics, with entity-swap tests showing early-layer features generalize much more (~80-92% overlap) than late-layer features (~0-50%).
metric: Replacement / Completeness scores (Neuronpedia) for concept-aligned subgraphs vs. geometric clustering baselines
target_value: concept-aligned subgraphs average 0.5394 Replacement and 0.8257 Completeness across 5 prompts, outperforming cosine-only and layer-adjacency clustering on behavioral metrics like Peak Token Consistency (0.425 vs. 0.183/0.301) and Activation Pattern Similarity (0.762 vs. 0.130/0.415)

title: Interpretable Fine Tuning Research Update and Working Prototype
primary_claim: ISaeRFT (Interpretable Sparse Autoencoder Representation Fine Tuning) — a technique that gradient-optimizes IA3-style learned scaling factors on SAE latents via a HuggingFace PeftModel — has a working prototype where DPO loss decreases significantly within as few as 20 training steps, though the research is at a very early stage with no major proof of concept yet on downstream tasks.
target_value: DPO loss goes down significantly in as few as 20 steps

title: Towards a Science of Evals for Sycophancy
primary_claim: The standard method of measuring LLM sycophancy (accuracy drop when an opinion decoy is added to a multiple-choice prompt) substantially overestimates true sycophancy, because most of the apparent effect is actually driven by a 'repetition bias' (the model favoring an answer merely because it is repeated in the prompt) rather than genuine agreement-seeking: in their Mistral-7B-Instruct/ARC-Easy setup, the naively measured 34-point accuracy drop reduces to a 22-point 'real sycophancy' effect once noise (~1 point) and repetition bias (~12 points) are subtracted out.
metric: accuracy on ARC-Easy under different decoy conditions
target_value: Baseline 75%; Opinion Bias 40.7% (-34.3pp); Noise (Opinion Decoy) 74.2% (-0.8pp); Repetition Bias 56.3% (-18.7pp from baseline); Noise (Repetition Decoy) 68.3% (-6.7pp from baseline); real sycophancy estimated at -22pp

title: Single Direction vs Low-Rank Refusal in Small LLMs
primary_claim: Refusal behavior in small instruction-tuned LLMs is compressed into a single dominant residual-stream direction in some models (Qwen, Gemma, Llama-3.1-8B) but is spread across a low-rank subspace in others (Llama-3.2-1B/3B, Phi-3-mini), so single-direction ablation achieves 80-96% compliance in the former group but only 15-39% in the latter.
metric: compliance rate (LLM-judge, harmful prompts, best single RV)
target_value: 80-96% for single-direction models (Qwen-1.8B, Qwen3-1.7B, Gemma-2B, Llama-3.1-8B) vs 15-39% for low-rank models (Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-3.2-3B, Phi-3-mini)

title: Research update: RL on Debate Games shows Proposal Accuracy uplift alongside Judge Hacking
primary_claim: Training debaters via RL in a Propose-Critique-Decide protocol improves Proposal accuracy on Hendrycks' MATH toward the RLVR ceiling and above the Consultancy floor with a weak Llama-3.1-8B judge, but the Critic simultaneously learns a 'judge hacking' spurious-critique strategy that causes Judge Alignment to decrease dramatically (driven by rising P(reject|correct)), even as Proposer accuracy continues to rise.
metric: Judge Alignment (correct-accept + incorrect-reject rate) over PCD-4 training steps, weak Llama judge
target_value: decreases dramatically after the first 50 steps, driven primarily by a rising P(reject|correct); Proposer accuracy nonetheless continues to rise
